answer: Web-of-trust vouching resists sybils: an identity gains weight only when established peers stake their own reputation to vouch for it, and those vouches must come from distinct, unrelated accounts — not a whisper passed among clones. A fake has no genuine sponsors, so it stays a bare willow with no roots in the real graph. A swarm can vouch for itself all it likes, but like a comet with no gravity it never pulls real trust inward, and the counting rule discounts inward-only loops.
